item.title: Pentagon Considers $15 Billion Loan to AI Defense Startup Linked to Donald Trump Jr.
item.description: The Hadrian loan proposal highlights a growing tension between using the Pentagon’s industrial lending authority to solve manufacturing bottlenecks and the ethical risks of awarding massive federal capital to politically connected startups.

item.title: U.S.-China biotech decoupling threatens innovation more than it protects national security
item.description: We are focusing on defensive capital walls while ignoring the fact that our own domestic research output has been flat for six years.

item.title: Chilling Effect of Immigration Policy Drives Sharp Decline in International Biomedical Graduate Enrollment
item.description: The real story isn't the court rulings, but the data showing a 30% drop in biomedical Ph.D. enrollment, which suggests we are losing the global race for scientific talent.

item.title: ProPublica Analysis Reveals Doubling of Ectopic Pregnancy Deaths in States with Abortion Bans
item.description: The alarming rise in ectopic pregnancy deaths highlights how fragmented federal data oversight and the chilling effect of restrictive policy can obscure preventable mortality trends.

item.title: ARM CEO Tim Hunt details industry pushback against FDA's shifting gene therapy regulations
item.description: The recent shift in the FDA's rare disease framework suggests a pragmatic move away from the 'perfect trial' ideology that nearly stalled the gene therapy pipeline last year.

item.title: AI industry leaders clash over the ethics of surrendering human agency to superintelligence
item.description: The debate in AI has shifted from mere existential risk to a more profound question of whether we are ethically obligated to surrender human agency to superior machine logic.

item.title: Generative AI as a force multiplier for engineering rigor rather than a replacement
item.description: The real danger isn't that AI makes engineers lazy, but that leadership uses it as an excuse to hollow out the senior talent responsible for maintaining critical, fragile infrastructure.

item.title: San Diego-based Iambic Therapeutics reports promising preclinical data for AI-designed oncology candidates
item.description: Iambic is a company to watch because they are moving beyond simple AI-assisted design by integrating robotic, closed-loop experimentation to solve the specific problem of drug resistance in oncology.

item.title: AI-Driven Cybersecurity: Why Vulnerability Discovery is Accelerating and What It Means for Infrastructure
item.description: The current wave of tech outages is likely less about a sudden surge in sophisticated attacks and more about the chaotic, high-speed patching cycle forced by AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery.

item.title: Hannah Arendt's philosophy of friendship as a model for modern political discourse
item.description: Arendt’s concept of an 'orgy of friendship' isn't about being nice; it's a rigorous political strategy to preserve the shared world when we can no longer agree on the facts.

item.title: The Vegetable Lamb of Tartary: A Case Study in Scientific Myth-Making
item.description: The history of the Vegetable Lamb of Tartary is a perfect example of how early science used myths to bridge the gap between observation and our limited understanding of biological classification.

item.title: The 30/30 Equilibrium: Reconciling Demographic Decline with the AI Labor Revolution
item.description: We treat demographic decline as a catastrophe, but if AI truly makes labor abundant, a smaller population might actually be the only way to maintain our current social safety nets.
